objective.value: Quantify the sizes of liquid smoke particulate in low gravity and relate the droplet-size distribution to the smoke generation and transport conditions; the reflight of SAME with a new material (Pyrell), broadened test conditions and improved diagnostics (M-pass) after the original TEM grids returned contaminated.

sources.note: PSI-101 Objectives: primary objective was to quantify the sizes of liquid smoke particulate in low gravity and relate droplet size distribution to smoke generation and transport; TEM grids from SAME were contaminated so SAME-R changed materials, conditions and diagnostics.
Urban et al. 2012 (SAME-2 particle morphology): the reflight built on the original flight by adding diagnostic measurements and expanding the test matrix.

relevance_notes.value: SAME-R is the reflight of the microgravity fire-detection study named in the brief. It provides the reduced-gravity smoke baseline used to evaluate how spacecraft smoke detectors respond to smoke from overheated materials, and its results indicate that detectors measuring more than one moment of the particle-size distribution may detect more reliably.

sources.note: Challenge brief, 'Background': fire detection was tested in microgravity through the SAME and SAME-R studies.
SAME-2 paper: broad smoke size distributions are expected from pre-fire overheat events; multi-moment detection may be more successful and false-alarm resistant than single-moment detectors.
PSI-101 Research Impacts: SAME-R provides the reduced-gravity baseline data against which future fire-detection technology can be evaluated.

notes: Primary source is the local PSI record data/source/psi/PSI-101.json and PSI-101.search.json (PSI-101 = SAME-R) plus the per-test table data/source/psi/tables/PSI-101.csv.
SAME-R is the reflight of SAME (PSI-102) and flew as 'SAME-2' on ISS Expedition 24, July-September 2010 (66 test points per PSI).

O2 concentration and pressure are not given in the PSI record or PSI-101.csv and were not stated in the readable NASA/NTRS sources, so they are left unknown (AGENTS.md rule 9). Overview PDFs commonly omit these.
conditions.airflow is left as in the seed because it is written by scripts/psi_apply_conditions.py from PSI-101.csv (inlet velocity 0 to 8.1 cm/s); the value is not hand-set (AGENTS.md rule 11).
fuel_phase is 'solid': the five SAME-R materials are solids heated below ignition (oxidative pyrolysis/smoldering), unlike SAME which used a liquid DBP reference. No flame is involved.

hardware.facility (MSG) is marked 'inferred': SAME operated in the Microgravity Science Glovebox and SAME-R reused the same SAME hardware, but no readable source states the SAME-R facility explicitly.
gravity_g is 0 g from the PSI Project Type 'Microgravity Investigation'; no partial-gravity claim is made (brief: PSI has no true partial-gravity combustion data).
Source conflicts: none found; the PSI record, PSI-101.csv and the NASA/NTRS documents agree on materials, conditions ranges and diagnostics.
